title: Packers acquire RB Kaleb Johnson in trade with Steelers
author: Matt Schneidman
content:
The Green Bay Packers traded with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday to acquire running back Kaleb Johnson, a team source confirmed. The source spoke on the condition of anonymity because they didn’t have permission to comment publicly.

Johnson, a 2025 third-round pick out of Iowa, provides depth at the position for Green Bay in case feature back Josh Jacobs is suspended. The Brown County District Attorney formally charged Jacobs with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property earlier this week. The NFL said in a statement that it is “closely monitoring all developments in the matter, which remains under review.”

The Packers already have MarShawn Lloyd as their No. 2 running back to take over if Jacobs misses time. Chris Brooks, a stout pass blocker, has been Green Bay’s No. 3 option. If Jacobs isn’t suspended before roster cuts are due at 5 p.m. CT on Sunday, the Packers could keep four running backs on the initial 53-man roster.

The trade ends Johnson’s brief and underwhelming tenure in Pittsburgh. The Steelers drafted Johnson in the third round of a talent-rich 2025 running back class. Johnson’s experience in Iowa’s wide-zone rushing attack appeared to make him a fit in an Arthur Smith offense. However, in Week 2 of his rookie season, Johnson made a costly special teams blunder. He allowed a kickoff to bounce over his head, gifting the Seahawks a bizarre touchdown.

Johnson never earned back the coaching staff’s trust. He carried the ball 28 times for 69 yards with no touchdowns last year. Johnson’s stock continued to fall this preseason. While he has a 6-1, 224-pound frame, his limited play speed (4.57 40-yard dash) was evident. He lacked explosiveness and rarely created more than what was blocked.

It’s a tough look for the Steelers to move on from a third-round pick just one year after he was drafted. It’s especially disappointing considering how other backs in the 2025 class have produced. Johnson was technically in a position battle for the RB3 job. Considering the Steelers have a steady 1-2 punch atop the depth chart in Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle, special teams was going to be a strong consideration. The way the Steelers split carries in the preseason suggested Johnson was likely on the outside looking in. Rather than cutting Johnson and having him sign elsewhere, Pittsburgh recouped some value with a trade.

Details of the trade have not yet been confirmed.

This story will be updated.
